clue.text: Driving manoeuvre, say doing a U-turn, with Gabriel getting clipped

indicators.note: turning back on itself, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: clipped means trimmed, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Gabriel is an archangel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A driver performs a U-turn while someone called Gabriel gets clipped by the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a U-turn' turns EG into GE; 'getting clipped' cuts the last L from ARCHANGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifting gear is a standard action performed while driving a car.

clue.text: Like pheasant, e.g. male having bright covering

indicators.note: the adjective covers, i.e. surrounds, the letter

parts.note: gay in its older sense means bright and cheerful

explanation.surface: A cock pheasant has bright plumage covering him.
explanation.walkthrough: The bright-plumaged male pheasant is a real picture, but 'e.g.' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds like pheasant taste strongly when hung, which is called gamey flavour.

clue.text: A Roman assassin moving right up in a tree

indicators.note: one letter shifts to another position in the name, here upwards in a down entry

parts.note: Brutus helped assassinate Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A Roman assassin climbs up into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving right up' takes R from BRUTUS and moves it up to the front, giving RBUTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is a species of the genus of this name.

clue.text: Dairy product, possible output of goat etc, it's said to make you smile

indicators.note: one possible thing produced by rearranging the letters given

parts.words: it's said to make you smile
parts.note: photographers ask you to say cheese to raise a smile

explanation.surface: Something a goat produces might be a dairy product that makes you smile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible output of' looks like goat's milk, but it rearranges GOATETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft curd made from milk is a type of milk-based food.

clue.text: A vice that's accepted

parts.note: greed is one of the deadly sins, a vice

explanation.surface: A vice that is tolerated by society.
explanation.definitionFit: Something approved by all parties has been consented to.

clue.text: A bloomer to stick around Eastern princess

indicators.note: the glue word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gum is glue, used to stick things
a rani is an Indian princess or queen

explanation.surface: An Eastern princess makes a blunder and sticks around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bloomer' suggests a mistake or loaf, but it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that blooms with flowers, a common garden pelargonium.

clue.text: Sign of official correspondence for electrical units

definitions.meaning: On Her Majesty's Service, printed on British government envelopes

explanation.walkthrough: OHMS stood for On Her Majesty's Service on British government mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an abbreviation stamped on state letters, and the plural of the unit of resistance.

clue.text: Musician playing rap hits

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: A musician performs rap hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who plays the harp is an instrumental performer.

clue.text: Show passion and skill embracing wife and lover

indicators.note: the verb embraces, i.e. holds inside it, the letter

parts.note: to seethe is to show intense emotion
art means skill

explanation.surface: A lover shows passion and skill embracing his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A beloved partner or romantic darling.

clue.text: Mafioso trashed Rome around summer time

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit around the time abbreviation
something trashed is wrecked, so the word Rome is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: BST is British Summer Time

explanation.surface: A gangster vandalises Rome during the summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Mafia is a gangster or criminal.

clue.text: Match official testimonial with no charge taken

indicators.note: taken away, so those letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a testimonial is a written character reference

explanation.surface: A referee's testimonial match is held without an entry fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A testimonial in British football is also a benefit match, which gives the surface its sporting look.
explanation.definitionFit: The referee is the umpire who controls a football match.

clue.text: One is going from one party to another — got travel info somehow

definitions.text: One is going from one party to another

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone moving between parties somehow got travel information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration, but it is a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector with no fixed allegiance switches support between political parties.

clue.text: Organised worker intrudes into a struggle

indicators.note: the words wrestle themselves into a new order, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A union man forces his way into a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Organised here means belonging to a labour union, a member of organised labour.

clue.text: Being madly made, does it rise when sheep's angry?

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, with the possessive giving the final S
hackles rise when an animal is angry

explanation.surface: Does a sheep's neck hair stand up when the animal is angry?
explanation.walkthrough: The hackle is the neck hair that rises on an angry animal; 'angry' completes that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rickety and shoddily put together is badly or carelessly constructed.

clue.text: She wrote 'A Transatlantic Decade'

parts.note: from across the Atlantic, i.e. American, US
a decade is ten years

explanation.surface: A female author penned a book called A Transatlantic Decade.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title looks like a book, but it splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen is a famous English female novelist.

clue.text: Aid to understanding foreign films being nuanced about it

indicators.note: the synonym wraps around the little word it

parts.note: subtle means finely nuanced
taken as written

explanation.surface: Foreign films become easier to follow when their captions are carefully nuanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Captions translating dialogue at the foot of the screen help viewers follow foreign cinema.

clue.text: Brag about amateur's support

indicators.note: the boasting word goes around the letter

parts.note: bluster is boastful talk
A abbreviates amateur

explanation.surface: Bragging about an amateur's support.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright post supporting a handrail.

clue.text: Aggressive youth had Nikes scuffed

indicators.note: scuffed means roughed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A thuggish lad's trainers were worn and scuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: Nikes are trainers, which suits the picture of a scuffed youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed young thug of British street subculture, often seen as violent.

clue.text: What reporter announces to create wow factor

definitions.meaning: a journalist introducing themselves might say ...
to ... people is to make them say wow

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, I'M PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dazzle or wow people is to make a strong favourable impression on them.

clue.text: Area west of New South Wales the Queen's come back to

indicators.note: in an across entry, west means placed to the left, before the next piece

parts.note: NSW is the Australian state's abbreviation
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The Queen returns to a region west of New South Wales in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: To reply or respond to someone is to come back to them.

clue.text: Military leader has news about half of army line

indicators.note: the news synonym goes around the other pieces

parts.note: word means news, as in 'any word?'

indicators.note: the first half of the word army is taken

explanation.surface: A general gets news about half the army's front line.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional commander ruling by force is a strongman or general.

clue.text: A Big Apple entertainment failing to start, in a haphazard way

parts.note: the Big Apple is New York, NY

indicators.note: its first letter is missing

parts.note: a show is entertainment

explanation.surface: A New York show fails to open properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Done carelessly, any old way, without method.

clue.text: Amount of business done by electronics company is sweet

parts.note: Apple is the computer and phone maker
turnover is a firm's total sales over a period

explanation.surface: A tech firm's sales figures are pleasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like an adjective on the turnover; it is the noun, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry filled with fruit is a pudding, which British speakers call a sweet.

clue.text: One's sore, getting left out of fashion

indicators.note: the letter is out of, i.e. removed from, the word

parts.note: style means fashion

explanation.surface: Someone is sore at being left out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflamed swelling on the eyelid is a painful spot.

clue.text: See Kent all out with extreme sharpness

indicators.note: all out of place, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Watch Kent's cricket side get bowled all out, with great sharpness.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county with a cricket team; 'all out' sounds like cricket, but it scrambles SEEKENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of an adjective meaning sharp, so it describes the greatest sharpness.

clue.text: Time Foreign Office should intervene in riot quickly

indicators.note: to intervene is to step in between, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a riot, in the sense of a hilarious event, is a hoot
FO is the British Foreign Office

explanation.surface: Diplomats should rush to step into a violent disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' reads as unrest, but it means something very funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in haste, at speed, is adverbial usage meaning in a hurry.

clue.text: Provide comfort and support mostly

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an easel is a stand supporting a painting

explanation.surface: Give comfort and support for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve or soothe someone is to make them comfortable.

clue.text: Keep protection with cutting through dreary escarpment

indicators.note: the letter splits the synonym, going inside it

parts.note: drab means dull and dreary
an escarpment is a long ridge of land

explanation.surface: A path cut through a gloomy cliff protects the stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb; it is a castle's central tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A liftable bridge over the moat guarded a castle stronghold.
